_source: Measured in 19.5 (console, batch) via twoway scatter mpg weight (sysuse auto) + graph describe + graph save + graph export, by scripts/extract_geometry_truth.do.

units.evidence_gph_header: xsize(6) ysize(4) -> '*! xsize: 6' and '*! ysize: 4' in the saved .gph
units.evidence_png: graph export width(600) of a 6x4in graph -> 600x400 px (ratio 1.5 = 6/4)
units.graph_describe_order: graph describe prints 'size:  4 x 6' for xsize(6) ysize(4): 'size: <ysize> x <xsize>' (height x width) -- NOT x-then-y

semantics.xsize_ysize: Overall GRAPH (canvas) dimensions in inches. Each is independent; supplying only xsize() leaves ysize at the scheme default (xsize(9) under stcolor -> 4.5 x 9).
semantics.xsize_ysize_validation: xsize(0) returns r(198) and xsize(-3) r(198).
semantics.aspectratio: Stata aspectratio(#) = PLOT REGION height / width. It does NOT change xsize/ysize: aspectratio(0.5) under stcolor still reports size 4.5 x 7.5 and the .gph records '.style.editstyle aspect_ratio(.5)' on the graph object only.

aspectratio_measured.note: A 6x6in graph; .Graph.plotregion1.xsize_ren and .ysize_ren, the plot region's drawn width and height in graph units. Confirms Stata aspectratio = height/width.

semantics.bokeh_aspect_ratio: Bokeh's Figure.aspect_ratio is width/height -- the RECIPROCAL of Stata's aspectratio(). Passing Stata's value straight through inverts the meaning.
semantics.scheme_graphsize_bare: A bare 'graphsize <n>' scheme entry does not affect graph dimensions when 'graphsize x'/'graphsize y' are also set. Probed with '#include s2color' + 'graphsize 3' -> 4 x 5.5 (s2color: 4 x 5.5).
semantics.scheme_graphsize_xy: 'graphsize x' is the default xsize (width, inches); 'graphsize y' is the default ysize (height, inches). Each is independent: '#include s2color' + 'graphsize y 2' -> 2 x 5.5.
semantics.override_precedence: An explicit xsize()/ysize() overrides the scheme's graphsize for that dimension only; the unspecified dimension keeps the scheme default (ysize(9) under stcolor -> 9 x 7.5).
semantics.stata_own_aspect_convention: ado/base/m/matrixgraph_g.class:197 computes 'local aspect = graphsize.x / graphsize.y' -- i.e. Stata itself treats x/y (width/height) as the aspect when converting graphsize to a ratio. This is the Bokeh-compatible direction.

fixture_cases_for_tests.note: graph size unchanged; plot region h/w = 0.5
